pages.headline: Jal Jeevan Mission extended to December 2028
pages.what: The Cabinet extended the mission with Rs 8.69 lakh crore, raising central assistance from Rs 2.08 to 3.59 lakh crore. It now stresses service delivery and digital tracking through Sujal Gaon ID.
key: Outlay Rs 8.69 lakh crore; central share Rs 3.59 lakh crore
Sujal Gaon ID under Sujalam Bharat
Funding 50:50; 90:10 for Himalayan and NE States
pages.static: Launched on 15 August 2019, JJM is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; drinking water is a State subject.

pages.headline: National Steering Committee for PM SETU
pages.what: The committee oversees the hub-and-spoke upgrade of ITIs under a Rs 60,000 crore scheme.
key: About four Spoke ITIs per Hub
pages.static: ITIs fall under the Directorate General of Training.

pages.headline: Jan Aushadhi Diwas 2026
pages.what: PMBJP supplies low-cost generics and plans 25,000 Kendras by March 2027.
pages.static: The Department of Pharmaceuticals is under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

pages.headline: FRA Cells become one-stop PMUs
pages.what: FRA Cells merge into PMUs under DAJGUA to cut silos.
pages.static: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises forest dwellers' rights.

pages.headline: CARA tightens adoption compliance
pages.what: CARA issued memorandums to State Adoption Resource Agencies to follow the JJ Act, 2015 and the Adoption Regulations, 2022 strictly. A surrendered child needs a two-month reconsideration period before being declared legally free for adoption.
key: CARA: statutory body under Ministry of Women and Child Development
Set up 1990; statutory status under JJ Act, 2015
Central Authority under Hague Convention (1993); India ratified 2003
CARINGS portal integrated with Mission Vatsalya portal
pages.static: The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 governs guardianship for communities whose personal laws do not recognise full adoption.
pages.angle: Trap: thinking HAMA adoptions need CARA registration.

pages.headline: NITI Aayog and UNICEF back IMPAct4Nutrition
pages.what: NITI Aayog and UNICEF India signed a Statement of Intent under the IMPAct4Nutrition platform to improve nutrition and health outcomes in aspirational districts and blocks. The platform links businesses with the POSHAN 2.0 movement.
key: Partners: NITI Aayog and UNICEF India
ACE Card: assets, CSR and employee engagement for nutrition
pages.static: POSHAN 2.0, or Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, is run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
pages.angle: Trap: treating I4N as a purely government scheme.

pages.headline: NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026
pages.what: Odisha, Goa and Jharkhand were Achievers; Arunachal led the smaller States.
key: Aspirational: West Bengal, Kerala, AP, Punjab
Arunachal tops NE and Himalayan group
pages.static: The FHI measures State finances; the 16th Finance Commission guides devolution.

pages.headline: India 116th in World Happiness Report
pages.what: India improved two places; Finland stays first.
pages.static: 20 March is the International Day of Happiness.

pages.headline: UN child mortality report: India's big fall
pages.what: India cut under-five mortality by 79 per cent between 1990 and 2024.
pages.static: U5MR is deaths under five per 1,000 live births.

pages.headline: Consumer Justice Report 2026: pendency up 21 per cent
pages.what: The India Justice Report's Consumer Justice Report 2026 found pendency in consumer commissions up 21 per cent between 2020 and 2024. Only 134 cases went to mediation, women's share among presidents and members fell from 35 to 29 per cent, and nearly half of State Commissions lacked a president.
key: Released by the India Justice Report
Women's share fell from 35 to 29 per cent
Nearly 50 per cent of State Commissions had no president
pages.static: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 set up the Central Consumer Protection Authority and a three-tier system of District, State and National Commissions.
pages.angle: Trap: reversing the women's share trend.
pages.remember: Consumer justice: pendency up, mediation near zero, women down.

pages.headline: NITI evaluation finds out-of-pocket spending under PM-JAY
pages.what: Beneficiaries still bore large costs, especially in private hospitals.
key: 65 per cent paid out of pocket
pages.static: PM-JAY is the world's largest publicly funded health assurance scheme.

pages.headline: India 54th in StartupBlink IBEI
pages.what: India ranked 54th, ahead of China at 85th.
key: US first, Singapore second, UK third
pages.static: The World Bank's Doing Business report was discontinued in 2021.

pages.headline: National Vaccination Day 2026
pages.what: Immunisation coverage at 98.4 per cent; HPV and Td vaccines launched.
pages.static: Mission Indradhanush strengthened routine immunisation.

pages.headline: World TB Day 2026
pages.what: India reported high treatment coverage but missed its elimination target.
key: Theme: Yes! We can End TB!
About 25 per cent of global cases
pages.static: The National TB Elimination Programme targeted 2025, five years ahead of the SDG goal.

pages.headline: Mahad Satyagraha centenary begins
pages.what: The Chavdar Tank march of 1927 began a rights movement for access to water.
key: 1937 Bombay HC opened tank to all
pages.static: Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

pages.headline: Ashmolean returns Thirumangai Alvar bronze
pages.what: A stolen 16th-century bronze was returned after tracing.
pages.static: The Alvars (Vaishnava) and Nayanars (Shaiva) led the Tamil bhakti movement.

pages.headline: Gyan Bharatam manuscript survey
pages.what: A three-month survey maps India's manuscripts.
pages.static: The National Mission for Manuscripts predates this.

pages.headline: ASI approves excavation at eight Tamil Nadu sites
pages.what: The Archaeological Survey of India approved excavations at eight Tamil Nadu sites: Keeladi, Adichanallur, Karivalamvanthanallur, Vellalore, Thelunganur, Nagapattinam, Pattinamarudur and Manikollai. Approvals come under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, 1959.
pages.static: The ASI works under the Ministry of Culture and administers the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.

pages.headline: Tribes Art Fest 2026
pages.what: Over 75 artists presented over 30 tribal art traditions.
pages.static: GI tags are granted under the GI Act, 1999.

pages.headline: Kalinjar hills declared Geo-Heritage Site
pages.what: GSI honoured the hills around Kalinjar.
pages.static: Geo-heritage sites preserve geological features.

pages.headline: India win T20 World Cup 2026
pages.what: India made 255/5 and bowled New Zealand out for 159.
key: Three titles; first on home soil
pages.static: The ICC is headquartered in Dubai.

pages.headline: ASMITA athletics league launched at 250 locations
pages.what: A nationwide athletics league for women was launched at 250 locations under ASMITA, a Khelo India initiative begun in 2021. ASMITA has drawn nearly 3 lakh women in 33 disciplines across 2,600 leagues.
key: ASMITA: Khelo India initiative for women's sports
pages.static: ASMITA expands to Achieving Sports Milestone by Inspiring Women Through Action.

pages.headline: Vairamuthu wins 60th Jnanpith
pages.what: The Tamil poet is the third Tamil laureate.
pages.static: Jnanpith is given for Eighth Schedule languages and English.

pages.headline: Sahitya Akademi Awards 2025 announced
pages.what: Awards in 24 languages across genres.
pages.static: Sahitya Akademi was founded in 1954.

pages.headline: Khelo India Tribal Games begin
pages.what: The first national multi-sport event for tribal athletes.
pages.static: Khelo India was launched in 2018.
